purpose: Presentation-only aliases for automatically generated Zoo Curator geographic Areas. Never authoritative for animal ranges or map geometry.

rules.note: area_name is intentionally shorter than the canonical map name where this can be done without changing geographic meaning.
rules.display_name_target: Prefer 1–2 words. Three words only when a shorter label would become unclear or geographically misleading.
rules.bioregion_generation: Suppress a bioregion Area when it adds no useful player-facing identity beyond its parent. Scientific/map data remains unchanged.
rules.branching_rule: A parent-to-bioregion visual layer is useful only where at least two distinct child Area identities can actually branch from that parent.
rules.hierarchy_visibility: Render a geographic level only when it adds a distinct useful identity. If parent and child cover the same generated enclosure set, collapse the parent. If a parent has no meaningful child branching, it may be the deepest generated Area.

semantic_audit.principle: Short display names must not materially broaden or narrow the canonical One Earth unit.
semantic_audit.reviewed_against: One Earth Bioregions Framework / realm and bioregion descriptions
semantic_audit.orinoco_region_note: Player-facing name for canonical One Earth subrealm 'Upper South America'; chosen to distinguish it clearly from Amazonia while retaining the canonical name separately.

inventory_viability_pass.borderline_policy: Retained. Four or more species makes generation possible; runtime spatial/enclosure rules decide whether an Area actually forms.

bioregion_inventory_viability.behavior: Bioregions below this inventory ceiling remain in the scientific/presentation registry but do not auto-generate as zoo Areas.
bioregion_inventory_viability.dynamic_runtime_note: Runtime Area formation still requires the normal spatial/enclosure threshold; inventory viability alone does not create an Area.
